title: Begrijpen / bedoelen / betekenen
summary: Three verbs that English speakers often confuse: begrijpen = to understand, bedoelen = to mean (intend), betekenen = to mean (signify).
rules: begrijpen — to understand. Subject is a person. 'Ik begrijp je niet.'
bedoelen — to mean / to intend. Subject is a person. 'Wat bedoel je?' (What do you mean?)
betekenen — to mean / to signify. Subject is usually a thing/word. 'Wat betekent dit woord?' (What does this word mean?)

examples.en: Do you understand what I'm saying?
